answer: Coordination-Priced Identity Windows.** Each agent gets one identity per window; new identities pay a price equal to the measured coordination cost they impose—the marginal messaging and settlement load their actions add to shared infrastructure, metered per sender. A zephyr of light activity stays cheap, but swarms of fresh identities trigger rising per-sender prices. Costs settle in juniper-denominated credits, and unused capacity decays to a nadir, so hoarded identities lose value.
